BEHIND THE OVERLAY

Evidence, made visible.

The app extracts straight segments from image gradients, then finds up to three projective direction families. Colored segments agree with a shared vanishing point; dashed rays show where they converge. Red segments are unexplained by the current fit.

The percentage is the share of detected edge length within the angular tolerance. It is not a probability that the image is correct. Images with multiple rotated objects may have more than three legitimate families, and a small set of lines can fit by chance.

Points outside the image are shown at the frame boundary with an arrow. Parallel directions are labeled “at infinity.” Sparse scenes produce an inconclusive result. Try changing the tolerance and comparing the original.

Processing runs on a resized copy (up to 720 pixels). No image is uploaded. Export saves the current view.
